title: Messi Just Went Web-Swinging Through Manhattan — and the World Cup's Wildest Crossover Wasn't on the Pitch
excerpt: Sony dropped a World Cup tie-in promo featuring the GOAT and Tom Holland's Peter Parker, and with advance bookings past 1 lakh tickets in India, Spider-Man: Brand New Day is building toward the country's biggest Marvel opening ever.
body:
Of all the things you expected from this World Cup, **Lionel Messi** screaming in mid-air while clinging to **Spider-Man** probably wasn't on the list.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=7733GKEaYEE</youtube>

And yet, on Tuesday, **Sony Pictures** dropped a promo for **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** that is now the most talked-about thing on the internet that doesn't involve a football and a net. In the short film, **Peter Parker** — played, as always, by **Tom Holland** — sits in a New York cafe when Messi walks in with a Spider-Man tracker, hunting for the web-slinger like he's tracking a through-ball. Parker's jaw drops. He trips over himself approaching the Argentine legend. Then he excuses himself, returns in full Spidey suit, and asks the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner the only question that matters:

> "You good with heights?"

What follows is sixty seconds of the GOAT being swung through the Manhattan skyline at terminal velocity, screaming like a man who has faced down every defence in Europe but was not prepared for this. It is absurd, joyful, and — because this is Messi — somehow still elegant.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DaNf54Uqw1d/



The timing is no accident. The **2026 FIFA World Cup** is raging across the United States right now, and Argentina — with Messi playing what will almost certainly be his final World Cup — are deep into the knockout stage. The crossover is Sony's sharpest piece of marketing in years: World Cup fever meets Marvel hype, and neither property is diminished by the association.

But Messi's appearance isn't just a celebrity cameo. The man is a genuine, documented Spider-Man fanatic. During his debut season with **Inter Miami**, he celebrated multiple goals with Marvel superhero poses — the Spider-Man web-shooting gesture went viral at least twice. His children are reportedly obsessed with the character. This promo isn't brand synergy. It's a love letter from a fan who happens to be the greatest footballer alive.

**In India**, the promo lands in especially fertile ground. Spider-Man is arguably the most popular Marvel character in the country, and the World Cup — with India's own campaign now over — has turned desi audiences into neutral-but-invested spectators of Messi's farewell tour. The collision of these two cultural obsessions in a single sixty-second spot is catnip for the Indian internet.

And the numbers suggest the excitement is translating to tickets. **Spider-Man: Brand New Day** has already crossed **1 lakh advance bookings** on PVR INOX alone, weeks before its **July 30** India release — a day before the US opening. The film will release in **six languages: English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada**, and has become the first Hollywood film to be mastered in **EPIQ**, India's homegrown premium large-format cinema experience, across all 12 screens nationwide.

Directed by **Destin Daniel Cretton** (*Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings*), Brand New Day picks up after the devastating conclusion of **No Way Home**, where the entire world forgot Peter Parker's identity. Tom Holland returns alongside **Zendaya**, **Sadie Sink**, **Jacob Batalon**, **Jon Bernthal**, and **Mark Ruffalo** in what promises to be the most emotionally grounded Spider-Man yet — which, given that the last film made everyone cry, is saying something.

Holland himself is having a summer. Two weeks before Spidey swings back, he'll star in **Christopher Nolan**'s **The Odyssey** (July 17), making him the rare actor anchoring two of the year's biggest blockbusters in the same month. When asked about Spider-Man's future, Holland recently said something that sent fans into orbit:

> "If I could do what Robert Downey Jr. did for me, mentoring the next generation — that's the dream."

**For diaspora audiences**, this is one to mark. India gets Brand New Day a full day early. The six-language rollout means your parents can watch it in Tamil and you can catch it in English and compare notes on the group chat. And if the Messi promo is any indication of the film's marketing swagger, the next month of teasers, character spots, and viral crossovers is going to be a ride.

One more detail worth noting: in the promo, when Peter Parker first sees Messi walk into the cafe, his reaction is pure, unfiltered starstruck awe. Tom Holland — who, let's remember, has met Robert Downey Jr., worked with Chris Pratt, and shared a screen with Benedict Cumberbatch — is playing a character who loses it at the sight of Lionel Messi.

Honestly? Same.
